facts.label: Leverage and coverage
facts.text: Net debt rose from USD 5,117 million at March 31, 2025 to USD 8,457 million at September 30, 2026, while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA fell from USD 1,669 million to USD 1,058 million. Reported net leverage therefore moved from 3.07x to 7.99x, with the peak of 8.10x at June 30, 2026. The mechanism is a working-capital and capital-spending build that was financed with short-term borrowings, at a time when fire losses and start-up costs cut reported earnings. Fiscal 2026 net debt was held down by USD 950 million of equity contributions from the shareholder, so the underlying build is larger than the net debt series shows. Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C10; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 111

facts.text: The six months to September 30, 2026 consumed USD 1,961 million before financing: operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 418 million and capital expenditure was USD 1,543 million, against USD 138 million of insurance proceeds. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against concern is that reported EBITDA is depressed by items the issuer treats as one-off: adjusted EBITDA of USD 508 million in the second quarter was 20% above the prior-year quarter, the Oswego hot mill restarted in June, and insurance recoveries of USD 519 million have been received cumulatively. If the Bay Minette plant moves to commercial shipments and capital spending falls as the issuer expects, adjusted net leverage near 4.62x would start to fall. The view would turn if working capital keeps absorbing cash or if start-up costs, which the issuer adds back, continue after commercial production begins. facts.label: Data quality and definitions
facts.text: Three definitions drive the numbers. EBITDA (Reported) is the issuer's unadjusted EBITDA, while Adjusted EBITDA adds back fire, restructuring, derivative and start-up items and deducts metal price lag gains. Total debt here is carrying value of USD 9,734 million, against contractual principal of USD 9,797 million, and the issuer's Adjusted Net Debt of USD 8,520 million is built on principal and cash, so it is USD 63 million higher than net debt on carrying value. The 10-K labels the Series 2026A Bonds as due June 2033 in its debt table while its own footnote and the later quarterly reports give a March 2033 tender date, and this answer uses the later reports' wording. - No balance sheet is printed at June 30, 2025 or September 30, 2025, because each interim report compares with the last fiscal year end, so prior-year interim leverage and liquidity cannot be shown. Severity: Low. The action is the quarterly report for September 30, 2025. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5

- The issuer states its net leverage ratio only in earnings releases and for four dates, so no stated ratio exists for December 31, 2025; the figures for that date in this answer are calculated on the issuer's components. Severity: Low. The action is the third-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings release. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; EX-99.1_2026-05-19_novelisq4fy26results.htm.jsonl, page 10

- Statement cells that print a dash are recorded as not supplied, never as zero, and a line that a period's statement does not print is recorded as not a line of that statement, for example loss on extinguishment of debt in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and the equity contribution line in the interim statements. Severity: Low. No action is needed unless a zero is wanted, which only the issuer can confirm. Basis: 10-Q_2026-06-30_nvl-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5

- The ABL Revolver draw is stated only as USD 2.3 billion, so the draw of USD 2,266 million is derived from short-term borrowings less the Brazil and China loans, and the split of short-term borrowings by currency is not stated. Severity: Low. The action is a facility-level borrowing schedule. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C29

- Confirmed supplier invoices under the supply chain finance programmes are stated in billions at interim dates (USD 1.5 billion at September 30, 2026 and USD 1.6 billion at June 30, 2026), so the exact interim balance, its trend and the guarantee the company gives for one programme are not quantified. Severity: Medium, because this float sits in accounts payable outside debt. The action is a roll-forward of confirmed obligations. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-06-30_nvl-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 132

- No source states the legal rank of the 2026 term loan facility, the Brazil and China loans, the Sierre loan or the finance leases, which together are USD 1,144 million of principal, so they are left out of the debt stack and of every secured and senior subtotal. Severity: Low. The action is the executed documents for those facilities. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–22; calculation C30

- The maturity ladder is the issuer's twelve-month buckets, with an undated last bucket of USD 2,658 million that includes the term loans, the 2033 notes and the tax-exempt bonds, so a dated wall by instrument is not built here. Severity: Low. The action is the instrument table in the debt note, used by Refinancing & LME. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17

- Several instrument terms are not stated in the notes and are marked not supplied in the instrument register: the currency of the Brazil loans, security and rank of the China, Sierre and Brazil loans, floors, the base of the term loan amortization and the amortization of two China loans. Severity: Low. The action is the underlying loan agreements. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–22

- Segment net sales are printed in the segment note but are not carried as a schedule in this answer; segment Adjusted EBITDA is in the key performance indicator table. Severity: Low. The action is a segment schedule in a later run. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–44

- Executed indentures and credit agreements are not in the source set, so covenant levels, baskets and the conditions of the ABL fixed charge test are known only from filing summaries and no covenant capacity is inferred. Severity: Low. The action is the executed documents. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 146–148 and 206–208

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Parent support is demonstrated but not committed. Hindalco subscribed USD 750 million of shares in December 2025 and USD 200 million in February 2026, USD 950 million in all, after the Oswego fires began, yet no guarantee, keepwell or support agreement for Novelis debt is stated, and the quarterly report warns that similar funding may not be made available in future. Equity paid in lowers the refinancing risk of the Bay Minette build; the absence of a commitment means that support is a pattern, not a claim. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 142; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C01

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against treating Hindalco's equity as a durable backstop is that a strategic parent has no stated obligation to Novelis creditors, took a USD 35 million return of capital in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, and that fiscal 2025 carried USD 10 million of costs for a postponed initial public offering, which shows a listing has been considered. Customer concentration is a second counterweight, with Ball at 18% of net sales and one supplier at 6% of metal purchases. The view would improve with a documented guarantee or support undertaking or a further equity injection, and it would worsen with a distribution or listing that takes capital out while net leverage of 4.7x is above the issuer's 3.5x target, or with commercial shipments from Bay Minette slipping past the first quarter of fiscal 2028. facts.label: Key findings

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Leverage is well above the issuer's own 3.5x target, and closing the gap needs both earnings growth and lower spending. The issuer's net leverage ratio was 2.9x at March 31, 2025, 4.1x at March 31, 2026, 4.5x at June 30, 2026 and 4.7x at September 30, 2026, so it has risen at every date the issuer states. At constant EBITDA, net debt would have to fall by USD 2,111.5 million to reach 3.5x, or Adjusted EBITDA would have to rise 32.95% at constant debt. On reported EBITDA, which carries fire losses and start-up costs, leverage is 7.99x. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a stretched view is that the cash burn is front-loaded by timing and choice. Capital expenditure guidance implies USD 557 million to USD 857 million in the second half against USD 1,543 million in the first, the Oswego hot mill is back in operation, USD 519 million of insurance recoveries has been recognized, Adjusted EBITDA per tonne is up 23.44%, the issuer states compliance with the covenants of the term loan facility, the revolver and the senior notes, and it guides to positive free cash flow in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027. A parent that injected USD 950 million after the fires began also signals support. The view would improve if adjusted free cash flow turns positive in that quarter, revolver availability stops falling and the issuer's net leverage ratio moves down from 4.7x. It would worsen if Bay Minette commercial shipments slip beyond the first quarter of fiscal 2028, working capital keeps absorbing cash as metal prices rise, revolver availability approaches the USD 300 million that the annual report's formula gives for a USD 3,000 million commitment, at which a fixed-charge test applies, or distributions resume while leverage is above 3.5x. facts.label: Company description and credit linkage

facts.label: Porter's five forces
facts.text: The threat of new entrants is low for flat-rolled sheet because a hot-mill plant costs billions of dollars, as Bay Minette shows at about USD 5 billion, and continuous casting is cheaper but serves a narrower product range. The threat of substitutes is moderate: aluminum has gained from glass, PET and steel on sustainability and weight, but the issuer notes that high aluminum prices can reverse that. Buyer power is high: the ten largest customers took 57% of fiscal 2026 net sales, Ball took 18%, some contracts carry no minimum volumes, and consolidation among customers increases their leverage. Supplier power is moderate: Rio Tinto, the primary metal supplier, was 6% of purchases in fiscal 2026, scrap is bought in a market where competition has risen, and gas is bought at market prices. Together, the forces cap pricing at the conversion premium and leave customer concentration as the main force that can move credit quality. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14, 17–18, 33, 188; calculation C23

facts.label: PEST analysis
facts.text: Political and regulatory factors are material, because trade policy changes cost and trade flows directly. Section 232 tariffs of up to 50% apply to imported aluminum, a temporary 10% global surcharge was applied in February 2026, tariffs reduced fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA by USD 143 million, and the issuer cut Kingston production in September 2026 for at least six months to avoid duties. The US antidumping dispute over Brazilian shipments holds a cash deposit of about USD 127 million that the issuer considers remote to lose. Credit implication: tariffs depress North American margin and add freight and working-capital cost, and Kingston curtailment shows management will trade volume for margin. facts.label: SWOT analysis
facts.text: Strengths in credit terms are the pass-through pricing model, recycling integration with 62.41% recycled metal, regional diversification across four segments, a beverage packaging anchor at 54.45% of fiscal 2026 net sales, and demonstrated parent equity of USD 950 million. Weaknesses are negative adjusted free cash flow of USD 1,804 million in the half, leverage of 4.7x against a 3.5x target, revolver-dependent liquidity of USD 2,038 million, and customer concentration of 57% in the ten largest customers. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are Bay Minette reaching commercial shipments in the first quarter of fiscal 2028, the second-half fall in capital spending, continued insurance recoveries and the efficiency plan. Threats are a slip in the Bay Minette ramp, tariff escalation, a reversal of scrap spreads, a strike or plant outage, and the withdrawal of supplier finance or parent funding. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48, 61; calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C24

facts.label: Financial profile and credit quality
facts.text: Scale and market position are strong: net sales of USD 18,434 million, a presence in all four regions through 29 facilities, and a leading position in beverage and automotive sheet that the issuer states. facts.text: Free cash flow stability is weak: adjusted free cash flow was negative in each of the last three fiscal years and widened from USD 75 million negative in fiscal 2024 to USD 737 million negative in fiscal 2025 and USD 2,377 million negative in fiscal 2026. The ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: the issuer extended maturities and raised USD 1,975 million of new debt between June 2025 and July 2026, but no rating, price or spread is supplied, so market access is read from the transactions completed. Liquidity position is average, and falling: USD 2,038 million, with a revolver maturing in 2031. Financial policy and governance is average: equity-supportive and transparent with a stated leverage goal, but the goal is exceeded, the owner controls the Board, and no guarantee is stated. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the decisive facts are the second-half step-down in capital spending, the Bay Minette ramp, and the flow of insurance recoveries. Management guides to positive free cash flow in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, deleveraging toward the end of the fiscal year, and commercial Bay Minette shipments in the first quarter of fiscal 2028, and it has kept the same timing, the end of fiscal 2027, at each of three reporting dates, in May, August and November 2026. Tailwinds are favorable scrap pricing, the Oswego restart in June 2026, recoveries still to come, and demand in beverage and aerospace. Headwinds are higher net tariffs, the Yeongju strike, weaker automotive and specialty shipments in the second quarter, and the expiry of the interest rate swaps in March 2027. Each tailwind lifts cash flow and each headwind lengthens the period of revolver use. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-19_novelisq4fy26results.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_novelisq1fy27results.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 46–48

facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over three to five years the credit depends on whether 600 kilotonnes of new North American capacity is filled at a conversion margin that supports the debt added to build it. The issuer expects growing long-term demand for beverage cans, automotive lightweighting and aerospace plate, but the annual report also notes that material substitution and tariffs can shift volume. The 2029 to 2031 maturities fall in this window, so the plant's contribution to Adjusted EBITDA has to be visible before those refinancings. A capacity addition of 16.87% of fiscal 2026 shipments can lift Adjusted EBITDA materially if it ramps, and keep leverage high if it does not. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The most plausible downside path is a slow Bay Minette ramp combined with metal prices that stay high, and it runs through working capital and the revolver, not through earnings collapse. The initiating condition is commercial shipments slipping beyond the first quarter of fiscal 2028 or ramping slowly while aluminum stays near USD 3,204 per tonne and the local premium near USD 1,242. The first operational break is that start-up costs, which Adjusted EBITDA excludes, and capital spending at the top of the USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.4 billion range persist. The financial transmission is that operating cash flow stays negative as inventories absorb cash, as they did in the first half when they took USD 733 million, so adjusted free cash flow stays negative and the revolver funds it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49, 65; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The consequence is that availability falls from USD 606 million toward the USD 300 million that the annual report's formula implies for the current commitment, at which a minimum fixed charge ratio of 1.25 to 1.0 would apply, a distance of USD 306 million if the wording is unchanged, and the issuer's net leverage ratio rises above 4.7x because Adjusted EBITDA does not grow into the debt. Management levers are lower discretionary capital spending, working capital release if metal prices fall, more insurance proceeds, the USD 800 million of uncommitted lines, and parent equity, none of which is committed. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis within twelve months if capital spending falls as guided, because the 6.78 months of runway at the first-half pace assumes no fall in spending and the revolver does not mature until 2031, but it is not sufficient to bring leverage back to the target unless the plant ramps. The observable triggers are availability below USD 300 million, a third-quarter adjusted free cash outflow, and a slip in the commercial shipment date. Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C06; calculation C11; calculation C12

facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Novelis presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, pass-through pricing, recycling integration and regional diversification, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow, leverage of 4.7x against a 3.5x target and revolver-dependent liquidity. Cash-flow durability appears weak in the near term and adequate if capital spending falls as guided, because EBITDA has not yet converted to cash. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the Bay Minette ramp, on leverage falling toward the target before 2029 to 2031, and on parent support that is not committed. The primary downside path is a delay in commercial shipments that keeps cash flow negative while the revolver funds it. The business profile cannot be benchmarked against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector because no peer set was supplied; a more definitive opinion would need covenant calculations, ratings, the second-half cash flow plan and the remaining plant spend. Credit view completed. Top risk: negative free cash flow until Bay Minette ships commercially. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 65; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 9–10; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C08

## Findings
### Bottom line

The supplied filings and releases support Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit on Novelis through September 30, 2026, so creditors can test leverage, liquidity and maturities, but not covenant headroom, ratings or market pricing. The quarterly results tie to the annual and trailing totals the issuer states, so the four fiscal quarters behind the latest twelve months can be assembled without gaps.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 8–10; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3

The set holds the annual report for the year ended March 31, 2026, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases, all for Novelis Inc. as one consolidated reporting entity that Hindalco owns indirectly. No executed indenture or credit agreement, agency rating, price quote, peer set or portfolio input was supplied, so covenant levels, security and guarantees are known only as the filings describe them. The quarter ended September 30, 2025 has no report of its own, and its balance sheet is not carried.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Net debt has risen at every balance-sheet date shown, to USD 8,457 million at September 30, 2026, and liquidity has fallen to its lowest of the five dates, so creditors depend on the Bay Minette start-up and insurance recoveries to turn cash flow positive.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C10; calculation C26

On reported EBITDA the last-twelve-months net leverage is 7.99x; on the issuer's adjusted EBITDA, which adds back USD 1,140 million of Oswego fire losses net of recoveries and deducts USD 574 million of metal price lag gains, it is 4.62x, close to the 4.7x the issuer states on its own definition. Cash interest paid is printed for fiscal years only, so interim cover cannot be built.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 8–10; calculation C15; calculation C18; calculation C10
### Leverage and coverage

Net debt rose from USD 5,117 million at March 31, 2025 to USD 8,457 million at September 30, 2026, while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA fell from USD 1,669 million to USD 1,058 million. Reported net leverage therefore moved from 3.07x to 7.99x, with the peak of 8.10x at June 30, 2026. The mechanism is a working-capital and capital-spending build that was financed with short-term borrowings, at a time when fire losses and start-up costs cut reported earnings. Fiscal 2026 net debt was held down by USD 950 million of equity contributions from the shareholder, so the underlying build is larger than the net debt series shows.
Basis: calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C10; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 111

On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the same net debt is 2.84x at March 31, 2025 and 4.62x at September 30, 2026, and each of the five dates is higher than the one before. The issuer targets about 3.5x during its investment cycle and says tariffs and the Oswego fires have pushed leverage above it. The adjusted measure also includes the share of joint-venture EBITDA the issuer manages on a proportional basis, so it is not a consolidated figure.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 99; calculation C21

Interest cover is available for fiscal years only: reported EBITDA covered cash interest paid 6.76x in FY2025 and 3.62x in FY2026, and adjusted EBITDA 7.30x and 6.80x. The fall in reported cover is the fire-loss effect, not a rise in interest paid, which was USD 247 million and USD 242 million.
Basis: calculation C22; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 112
### Cash flow and liquidity

The six months to September 30, 2026 consumed USD 1,961 million before financing: operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 418 million and capital expenditure was USD 1,543 million, against USD 138 million of insurance proceeds. Inventories absorbed USD 733 million, and the issuer attributes the outflow to unfavorable working capital changes and the Oswego fires. Net revolving borrowing of USD 1,330 million, almost all on the ABL Revolver, funded the gap, and the USD 500 million 2026 term loan arrived in July. Short-term borrowings of USD 2,631 million now exceed cash of USD 1,277 million, and principal due within twelve months is USD 2,704 million, most of it short-term borrowings, of which the ABL Revolver draw is USD 2,266 million on a facility that matures in 2031.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; calculation C27

Liquidity of USD 2,038 million at September 30, 2026 compares with USD 2,756 million at March 31, 2026, and committed availability fell from USD 1,502 million to USD 761 million. Confirmed supplier invoices under supply chain finance were USD 1.5 billion at September 30, 2026 and USD 1,262 million at March 31, 2026; they sit in accounts payable, not debt, and are float that would have to be funded if the programmes shrank.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 132; calculation C23
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against concern is that reported EBITDA is depressed by items the issuer treats as one-off: adjusted EBITDA of USD 508 million in the second quarter was 20% above the prior-year quarter, the Oswego hot mill restarted in June, and insurance recoveries of USD 519 million have been received cumulatively. If the Bay Minette plant moves to commercial shipments and capital spending falls as the issuer expects, adjusted net leverage near 4.62x would start to fall. The view would turn if working capital keeps absorbing cash or if start-up costs, which the issuer adds back, continue after commercial production begins.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 67–68
### Data quality and definitions

Three definitions drive the numbers. EBITDA (Reported) is the issuer's unadjusted EBITDA, while Adjusted EBITDA adds back fire, restructuring, derivative and start-up items and deducts metal price lag gains. Total debt here is carrying value of USD 9,734 million, against contractual principal of USD 9,797 million, and the issuer's Adjusted Net Debt of USD 8,520 million is built on principal and cash, so it is USD 63 million higher than net debt on carrying value. The 10-K labels the Series 2026A Bonds as due June 2033 in its debt table while its own footnote and the later quarterly reports give a March 2033 tender date, and this answer uses the later reports' wording.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 145; calculation C24; calculation C25

- Cash interest paid is not stated for any interim period, so interest cover cannot be calculated for the last twelve months at December 31, 2025, June 30, 2026 or September 30, 2026. Severity: Medium. The action that would close it is an interim disclosure of interest paid.

- The balance sheet at March 31, 2024 is not printed, so total debt, net debt and leverage for FY2024 are not calculable; only cash at that date is stated, in the cash flow statement. Severity: Low. The action is the prior annual report.

- No balance sheet is printed at June 30, 2025 or September 30, 2025, because each interim report compares with the last fiscal year end, so prior-year interim leverage and liquidity cannot be shown. Severity: Low. The action is the quarterly report for September 30, 2025.

- The issuer states its net leverage ratio only in earnings releases and for four dates, so no stated ratio exists for December 31, 2025; the figures for that date in this answer are calculated on the issuer's components. Severity: Low. The action is the third-quarter fiscal 2026 earnings release.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; EX-99.1_2026-05-19_novelisq4fy26results.htm.jsonl, page 10

Severity: Low. No action is needed unless a zero is wanted, which only the issuer can confirm.

- The ABL Revolver draw is stated only as USD 2.3 billion, so the draw of USD 2,266 million is derived from short-term borrowings less the Brazil and China loans, and the split of short-term borrowings by currency is not stated. Severity: Low. The action is a facility-level borrowing schedule.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C29

- Confirmed supplier invoices under the supply chain finance programmes are stated in billions at interim dates (USD 1.5 billion at September 30, 2026 and USD 1.6 billion at June 30, 2026), so the exact interim balance, its trend and the guarantee the company gives for one programme are not quantified. Severity: Medium, because this float sits in accounts payable outside debt. The action is a roll-forward of confirmed obligations.

- No source states the legal rank of the 2026 term loan facility, the Brazil and China loans, the Sierre loan or the finance leases, which together are USD 1,144 million of principal, so they are left out of the debt stack and of every secured and senior subtotal. Severity: Low. The action is the executed documents for those facilities.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–22; calculation C30

- The maturity ladder is the issuer's twelve-month buckets, with an undated last bucket of USD 2,658 million that includes the term loans, the 2033 notes and the tax-exempt bonds, so a dated wall by instrument is not built here. Severity: Low. The action is the instrument table in the debt note, used by Refinancing & LME.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17

- Several instrument terms are not stated in the notes and are marked not supplied in the instrument register: the currency of the Brazil loans, security and rank of the China, Sierre and Brazil loans, floors, the base of the term loan amortization and the amortization of two China loans. Severity: Low. The action is the underlying loan agreements.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–22

- Segment net sales are printed in the segment note but are not carried as a schedule in this answer; segment Adjusted EBITDA is in the key performance indicator table. Severity: Low. The action is a segment schedule in a later run.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–44

- Executed indentures and credit agreements are not in the source set, so covenant levels, baskets and the conditions of the ABL fixed charge test are known only from filing summaries and no covenant capacity is inferred. Severity: Low. The action is the executed documents.

spans.text: ## Request

Business & governance for Novelis Inc. (novelis-inc), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the company, its operating model, ownership and control, disclosed financings and capital allocation, and the governance and sponsor behaviour that matters to creditors, from the supplied filings and earnings releases.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Novelis is a scaled, diversified aluminum producer owned entirely by Hindalco, which put USD 950 million of equity into it in fiscal 2026, so creditors have visible parent support, but it funds a USD 5 billion Bay Minette plant that has yet to produce cash.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 142; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65; calculation C01

The support is shown by equity paid in, not by a guarantee of Novelis debt, and the filings say further contributions are not assured. Hindalco appoints every director, related-party dealings are small, and Ball alone is 18% of fiscal 2026 net sales. Sponsor and governance risk is assessed as Medium.
### Key findings

- Parent support is demonstrated but not committed. Hindalco subscribed USD 750 million of shares in December 2025 and USD 200 million in February 2026, USD 950 million in all, after the Oswego fires began, yet no guarantee, keepwell or support agreement for Novelis debt is stated, and the quarterly report warns that similar funding may not be made available in future. Equity paid in lowers the refinancing risk of the Bay Minette build; the absence of a commitment means that support is a pattern, not a claim.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 142; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C01

- The business is diversified by region and end market but concentrated by customer. Beverage packaging was 54.45% of fiscal 2026 net sales and 56.14% of the first half of fiscal 2027, Ball was 18% of net sales, and the four regions contributed 26.43%, 23.03%, 18.89% and 31.65% of segment Adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2026. Pricing passes aluminum costs through, so earnings follow conversion margins, but each price rise lifts working capital.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 188 and 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 44 and 49; calculation C02; calculation C04

- Earnings recovery rests on two projects. The Oswego hot mill restarted in June 2026 and USD 519 million of net insurance recoveries had been received by September 30, 2026, against an issuer estimate in May 2026 of about USD 1.7 billion of negative cash flow before recoveries. North America fell from 35.61% of segment Adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2025 to 26.43% in fiscal 2026 and 25.02% in the first half of fiscal 2027, and Bay Minette, which produced its first cold mill coil in September 2026, expects commercial shipments in the first quarter of fiscal 2028.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36 and 48; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 70; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2 and 10; calculation C03

- Capital allocation is investment-led, with small and discretionary distributions. Capital expenditure guidance for fiscal 2027 is USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.4 billion, of which USD 1,543 million was spent in the first half; returns of capital to the shareholder were USD 35 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, USD 100 million in fiscal 2024 and none in fiscal 2025 or the first half of fiscal 2027. The framework aims to return 8% to 10% of post-maintenance adjusted free cash flow, at the Board's discretion and subject to the debt instruments.

- Financing has been extended in size and tenor, but near-term liquidity still leans on the ABL Revolver. New funding since June 2025 includes USD 750 million of 2033 notes, USD 725 million of tax-exempt bonds, a USD 500 million term loan in July 2026 and USD 950 million of equity, and the ABL Revolver commitment rose by USD 1 billion in two steps to USD 3.0 billion with maturity moved to June 2031.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–23; calculation C01; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08

- Governance is simple and transparent but not independent of the parent. All eight directors were appointed by Hindalco, three have Hindalco ties that the company treats as related-party relationships, the two standing committees are Audit and Compensation, and the auditor has served since 2006. Related-party transactions are not material, and the new brand licence caps the royalty at USD 24 million for fiscal 2027.

- About a fifth of sales sits outside the guarantor group. Non-guarantor subsidiaries were 20% of net sales and 18% of Adjusted EBITDA for the first half of fiscal 2027 and 11% of assets, with USD 2.2 billion of debt and other liabilities; the guarantor list itself is not supplied.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 64–65
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against treating Hindalco's equity as a durable backstop is that a strategic parent has no stated obligation to Novelis creditors, took a USD 35 million return of capital in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, and that fiscal 2025 carried USD 10 million of costs for a postponed initial public offering, which shows a listing has been considered. Customer concentration is a second counterweight, with Ball at 18% of net sales and one supplier at 6% of metal purchases. The view would improve with a documented guarantee or support undertaking or a further equity injection, and it would worsen with a distribution or listing that takes capital out while net leverage of 4.7x is above the issuer's 3.5x target, or with commercial shipments from Bay Minette slipping past the first quarter of fiscal 2028.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 142, 173 and 188; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3
### Limitations

- The executed indentures, credit agreements and guarantee documents were not supplied, so the restricted-payment and guarantee terms that show how much value the parent could take out are not established; this limits the Medium risk level, which rests on behaviour, not legal capacity.

- No agency rating, market price or support agreement exists in the set for this strategic parent, so willingness is read only from disclosed actions; a documented undertaking could move the level either way.
- The list of subsidiaries and the guarantor group are not supplied, so the guarantor perimeter rests on percentages and the structural reading of who owes what to whom is incomplete.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 64–65
- No single transaction is declared in the run settings, so the transaction summary lists the financings and equity contributions the filings disclose, not one deal with sources and uses.
### Company and operating model

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The run settings declare no single transaction, so this section lists the financings and equity contributions the filings disclose. New debt since June 2025 totals USD 1,975 million: USD 400 million of Series 2025A Bonds in June 2025, USD 750 million of 6.375% senior notes due 2033 on August 18, 2025, USD 100 million of Series 2025B Bonds in September 2025, USD 225 million of Series 2026A Bonds in March 2026 and a USD 500 million unsecured term loan on July 23, 2026. The three tax-exempt bond series, USD 725 million in all, were loaned to Novelis Corporation to finance Bay Minette and are guaranteed on a senior unsecured basis by Novelis Inc. and certain subsidiaries.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–23; calculation C06; calculation C08

The 2033 notes were issued with a cash tender offer for the 2026 notes, which bought USD 737 million of the USD 750 million outstanding and left USD 13 million to mature on November 15, 2026. The term loan was repriced on September 15, 2025, lowering its margin from 2.00% to 1.75%, and the ABL Revolver commitment was raised on February 19, 2026 and June 16, 2026 to USD 3.0 billion, with maturity moved to June 16, 2031. On the equity side, Hindalco paid USD 750 million on December 23, 2025 and USD 200 million on February 18, 2026 for new shares, which left ownership unchanged.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 142 and 150; calculation C01

A new brand and intellectual property licence with Birla Group Holdings Private Limited was approved on August 4, 2026 and took effect on July 1, 2026, with fiscal 2027 royalties capped at USD 24 million and USD 11 million recognised in the second quarter.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

Fundamental credit for Novelis Inc. (novelis-inc), as of 2026-11-05, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the consolidated profile of Novelis Inc. and its subsidiaries: business and cost model, capital intensity, financial profile, outlook, downside path, ranked drivers and monitoring triggers, drawn from the supplied annual report, quarterly reports and earnings releases and the three earlier answers of this run.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Novelis is a scaled, recycling-integrated aluminum roller whose credit is stretched but not distressed: negative free cash flow from the Bay Minette build has lifted leverage and drained revolver availability, so creditors rely on the revolver and parent equity until cash flow turns.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 61–65; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C10

Net leverage on the issuer's own measure is 4.7x against a 3.5x target, adjusted free cash flow was an outflow of USD 1,804 million in the first half of fiscal 2027, and liquidity fell to USD 2,038 million from USD 2,756 million in six months. Scheduled maturities are small until April 2029, but management's return to positive free cash flow in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027 is an expectation, and the parent has made no commitment to repeat its USD 950 million equity injection.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 65; calculation C02; calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C22
### Key findings

- Operating risk is moderate: the business earns a defensible margin per tonne, and the pressure is cash timing, not earnings power. Adjusted EBITDA per tonne was USD 553 in the second quarter against USD 448 a year earlier, up 23.44%, and last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,831 million is above the fiscal 2026 figure of USD 1,645 million. Conversion pricing passes metal costs to customers, so earnings follow conversion margin and scrap spreads, but each rise in the aluminum price lifts inventories and receivables before cash is collected.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation C15

- Free cash flow is the weakest dimension and the cause of the leverage problem. Adjusted free cash flow was an outflow of USD 1,804 million in the first half of fiscal 2027 and USD 3,682 million over the last twelve months, and net debt rose by USD 1,801 million in six months, almost exactly the cash outflow. Operating cash flow before working capital was USD 555 million against capital expenditure of USD 1,543 million, so even a neutral working-capital half would not have covered spending.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 85; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C10

- Leverage is well above the issuer's own 3.5x target, and closing the gap needs both earnings growth and lower spending. The issuer's net leverage ratio was 2.9x at March 31, 2025, 4.1x at March 31, 2026, 4.5x at June 30, 2026 and 4.7x at September 30, 2026, so it has risen at every date the issuer states. At constant EBITDA, net debt would have to fall by USD 2,111.5 million to reach 3.5x, or Adjusted EBITDA would have to rise 32.95% at constant debt. On reported EBITDA, which carries fire losses and start-up costs, leverage is 7.99x.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_novelisq1fy27results.htm.jsonl, page 10; EX-99.1_2026-05-19_novelisq4fy26results.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65; calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03

- Liquidity is adequate for the next twelve months only if the guided fall in capital spending happens, and it is revolver-dependent. Liquidity fell to USD 2,038 million from USD 2,756 million at March 31, 2026 because committed availability fell 49.33% as the revolver draw rose to USD 2,266 million. Debt due within twelve months is USD 2,704 million, of which only USD 438 million is not the revolver, and liquidity covers that 4.65 times. At the first-half pace of cash outflow, liquidity would last about 6.78 months, which is why the second-half step-down in capital spending is the central test.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C07; calculation C12

- Refinancing risk is low until 2029 but concentrates in 2029 to 2031. Scheduled maturities before 2029 are small: USD 13 million of notes in November 2026, local loans of USD 200 million in 2027 and the USD 500 million 2026 term loan in July 2028. Then USD 5,961 million, or 60.85% of principal, falls due in 2029 to 2031 when the revolver is counted at its June 2031 maturity, including USD 2,350 million of January 2030 senior notes. Market access then depends on leverage having fallen toward the target, which is the issuer's stated plan and not yet a result.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–21; calculation C22

- The earnings recovery rests on items that are partly temporary. Business-interruption insurance recoveries were USD 39 million, or 7.68%, of second-quarter Adjusted EBITDA, scrap-price benefits are market driven, and start-up costs of USD 69 million over twelve months are added back although they are real cash costs until Bay Minette ships commercially. The issuer's adjustments also deduct USD 574 million of metal price lag gains, so they cut both ways, but the USD 773 million gap between reported and adjusted EBITDA is dominated by a USD 1,140 million fire add-back.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36; calculation C14

- Parent support is a demonstrated pattern, not a commitment. Hindalco paid USD 950 million of equity in fiscal 2026 after the fires began, but no guarantee of Novelis debt is stated, although the revolver agreement names the shareholder as a third party security provider in a role the notes do not describe, and the issuer says similar funding may not be made available in future. The capital allocation framework guides 8% to 10% of post-maintenance adjusted free cash flow to the shareholder at the Board's discretion, which implies no return while that cash flow is negative.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 65; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 142, 208; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- Customer and trade exposure is concentrated. The ten largest customers took 57% of fiscal 2026 net sales against 41% a year earlier, Ball alone took 18%, US tariffs cut fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA by USD 143 million, and the issuer curtailed Kingston production in September 2026 to avoid duties. These exposures reduce pricing power in a downturn and tie North American margin to trade policy.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 188; EX-99.1_2026-05-19_novelisq4fy26results.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; calculation C23

- Claims outside the debt figure are modest except supplier finance and purchase commitments. Net pension and retiree medical liabilities are USD 493 million and lease payment obligations USD 173 million, confirmed supplier invoices rose 48.47% to USD 1,262 million in fiscal 2026, and purchase obligations were USD 17.2 billion at March 31, 2026, with USD 7.6 billion due within twelve months. None of these is in the debt figure, and supplier finance is a funding float that would need to be replaced if the programmes shrank.

Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 83–84; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 132; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 159–161; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a stretched view is that the cash burn is front-loaded by timing and choice. Capital expenditure guidance implies USD 557 million to USD 857 million in the second half against USD 1,543 million in the first, the Oswego hot mill is back in operation, USD 519 million of insurance recoveries has been recognized, Adjusted EBITDA per tonne is up 23.44%, the issuer states compliance with the covenants of the term loan facility, the revolver and the senior notes, and it guides to positive free cash flow in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027. A parent that injected USD 950 million after the fires began also signals support. The view would improve if adjusted free cash flow turns positive in that quarter, revolver availability stops falling and the issuer's net leverage ratio moves down from 4.7x. It would worsen if Bay Minette commercial shipments slip beyond the first quarter of fiscal 2028, working capital keeps absorbing cash as metal prices rise, revolver availability approaches the USD 300 million that the annual report's formula gives for a USD 3,000 million commitment, at which a fixed-charge test applies, or distributions resume while leverage is above 3.5x.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 148; calculation C06; calculation C11; calculation C14; calculation C16
### Limitations

- The conclusion that liquidity is adequate depends on management's guided return to positive free cash flow in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, and no second-half cash flow bridge or remaining Bay Minette spend is supplied, so a miss would move the liquidity view toward stressed once revolver availability nears its test level.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_novelisq1fy27results.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C11

- The distance to the revolver's fixed-charge test is indicative only: the annual report wording predates the June 2026 amendment, and neither the borrowing base nor the fixed-charge ratio is supplied, so covenant headroom is not established and the liquidity conclusion could be too generous if the amended trigger sits above USD 300 million.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 18; calculation C06

- The 4.7x leverage ratio and the Adjusted EBITDA behind it rest on issuer-defined add-backs, including Bay Minette start-up costs that will stop being excluded at a date the issuer does not state, so if those costs persist after commercial production begins the improvement in adjusted leverage will be overstated.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41, 67; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C14

- No peer set, agency rating or market price is supplied, so the comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers is qualitative and each strong, average or weak reading of a profile dimension is absolute, not relative to a benchmark.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- Insurance policy limits and the amount of recoveries still to come are not stated, so how much of the estimated USD 1.7 billion negative cash flow from the fires will be recovered is not established, and a lower recovery would lengthen the cash gap that the revolver now funds.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48; calculation C16
### Strengths and weaknesses
The five main supports of the credit, in order of weight, are these.

- Pass-through conversion pricing, scale and recycling give earnings per tonne that have already recovered. Adjusted EBITDA per tonne was USD 553 in the second quarter, up 23.44%, and recycled metal was about 62.41% of the metal the issuer purchased or tolled in fiscal 2026, which both lowers energy use and reduces dependence on primary metal. Pricing that passes the metal cost to customers means a rise in the aluminum price does not squeeze the conversion margin, so earnings power should return to debt service once capital spending falls.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 15, 18; calculation C15; calculation C24

- Regional and end-market diversification limited the damage from the Oswego fires. Beverage packaging was 54.45% of fiscal 2026 net sales, and while North America Adjusted EBITDA fell to 25.02% of the segment total in the first half of fiscal 2027, South America grew 52.42% and Europe 33.77% in the same half. Group Adjusted EBITDA therefore rose 22.20% in the half while the Oswego plant was down, which is the evidence that no single plant or region carries the credit.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 10–11; calculation C17

- The maturity profile was lengthened by the 2025 and 2026 financings. The revolver commitment is USD 3,000 million to June 2031, tax-exempt bonds of USD 725 million finance Bay Minette with tender dates in 2032 and 2033, and scheduled maturities before 2029 are USD 713 million, or 7.28% of principal. Little of the debt falls due before the plant should be producing, so refinancing pressure is back-loaded.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–23; calculation C22

- The parent has shown willingness to put in equity. Hindalco subscribed USD 950 million of shares in fiscal 2026, after the fires began, which cut the borrowing needed for Bay Minette, though no commitment to repeat is stated.

- Insurance recoveries and a cost programme cushion the fire and tariff losses. USD 519 million of recoveries has been recognized to September 30, 2026, and the 2025 Efficiency Plan exited fiscal 2026 with more than USD 200 million of run-rate savings against a target of USD 350 million to USD 400 million a year by the end of fiscal 2028, which supports margin if volumes normalize.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35–36, 47–48; calculation C16
The five main weaknesses, in order of weight, are these.

- Free cash flow is deeply negative. Adjusted free cash flow was an outflow of USD 1,804 million in the first half of fiscal 2027 and USD 3,682 million over twelve months, because capital expenditure of USD 1,543 million exceeded operating cash flow before working capital of USD 555 million and working capital absorbed a further USD 973 million. Debt funded the gap, so net debt rose USD 1,801 million in six months.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation C08; calculation C09; calculation C10

- Leverage is above the issuer's target on every measure. The issuer's net leverage ratio is 4.7x against 3.5x, net debt to reported EBITDA is 7.99x, and returning to the target at constant debt needs Adjusted EBITDA to rise 32.95%, so deleveraging depends on both the Bay Minette ramp and falling spending.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 9–10; calculation C01; calculation C03

- Liquidity is thinner and more dependent on the revolver than six months ago. Committed availability fell 49.33% in six months to USD 761 million, short-term borrowings of USD 2,631 million exceed cash of USD 1,277 million, and the USD 800 million of uncommitted lines are not counted in liquidity and can be withdrawn. Less cushion means a smaller shock can reach the revolver's fixed-charge test.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; calculation C04; calculation C06

- Earnings quality and execution risk are both high. Insurance recoveries were 7.68% of second-quarter Adjusted EBITDA, scrap-price benefits are market driven, start-up costs are added back, and the free cash flow turn depends on Bay Minette reaching commercial shipments in the first quarter of fiscal 2028. A slip would extend the period of negative cash flow while debt keeps rising.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C14

- Customer, trade and funding-float exposures are concentrated. The ten largest customers took 57% of fiscal 2026 net sales, tariffs cost USD 143 million of fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA, and confirmed supplier invoices of USD 1,262 million at March 31, 2026 sit in payables outside debt. A loss of a large customer or a tightening of supplier finance would hit earnings or liquidity without any change in reported debt.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 33, 132; EX-99.1_2026-05-19_novelisq4fy26results.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C18; calculation C23

### Company description and credit linkage

Novelis rolls and recycles aluminum into sheet, plate and light gauge products for beverage packaging, automotive, aerospace and specialty customers. It operates 29 facilities in nine countries, 15 of them with recycling, and reported fiscal 2026 net sales of USD 18,434 million and rolled product shipments of 3,557 kilotonnes. Beverage packaging was 54.45% of fiscal 2026 net sales, specialty 21.48%, automotive 20.11% and aerospace and industrial plate 3.96%. The company was formed in Canada in 2004, was acquired by Hindalco in 2007 and shows no acquisition or large disposal in the period reviewed; the large strategic events are the Bay Minette greenfield plant and the two Oswego fires.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 188; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The model supports cash-flow visibility because most products are priced as an aluminum base plus a local premium plus a conversion premium, so metal price changes pass through, and large customers qualify their suppliers over many months, which makes volumes sticky. It weakens debt service capacity in two ways: the pass-through lifts working capital when metal prices rise, and some customer contracts carry no minimum purchase volume. Seasonality lowers third-quarter shipments, so the December quarter carries the lowest volumes.
### Ownership and group structure

All 606,333,333 common shares are held directly by AV Minerals (Netherlands) N.V. and indirectly by Hindalco, and Hindalco appointed all eight directors. The perimeter used throughout is Novelis Inc. and its subsidiaries on a consolidated basis; no Hindalco or AV Minerals figure was supplied and none is used. The US dollar senior notes were issued by Novelis Corporation and the euro notes by Novelis Sheet Ingot GmbH, all guaranteed jointly and severally on a senior unsecured basis by Novelis Inc. and certain subsidiaries, while the senior secured facilities are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries and secured by substantially all assets of the company and the guarantors. The annual report's exhibit index names AV Minerals (Netherlands) N.V., the direct shareholder, and Novelis Italia S.p.A. as third party security providers under the revolver agreement, and names Novelis Holdings Inc. as borrower of the term loan with Novelis Inc. as intermediate holdings company, but the notes do not describe what security the shareholder gives, so its role in the secured package is an open point and not a stated guarantee.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 146, 148, 150, 208; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The behaviour that matters to creditors is that the owner supports capital projects with equity rather than extracting cash: USD 950 million came in during fiscal 2026 against a return of capital of USD 35 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, none has been paid in fiscal 2027, and the new brand licence royalty is capped at USD 24 million for fiscal 2027. The framework that guides 8% to 10% of post-maintenance adjusted free cash flow to the shareholder is discretionary and subject to debt covenants. Structurally, secured debt of USD 3,497 million, or 35.69% of principal, ranks ahead of the unsecured notes in the guarantor group, and subsidiaries outside the guarantor group hold USD 2.2 billion of debt and other liabilities against USD 3.7 billion of assets, so cash and assets there serve local creditors first.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 64, 65; calculation C21; calculation C26
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is recurring and pass-through priced, cyclical in automotive and specialty, and concentrated by customer. Rolled product shipments fell 5% in fiscal 2026 to 3,557 kilotonnes with the Oswego outage and were down 3.62% in the first half of fiscal 2027, while second-quarter net sales rose 25% mainly because the aluminum price rose. Higher beverage packaging and aerospace shipments were offset by lower automotive and specialty shipments in the second quarter. The ten largest customers took 57% of fiscal 2026 net sales and some contracts are renegotiated periodically, so a lost contract would show up in volume before price.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 11; EX-99.1_2026-05-19_novelisq4fy26results.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 33; calculation C28

Pricing power is limited to the conversion premium and to qualification barriers, because customers can switch material when aluminum becomes dear: the annual report names glass, PET plastic and steel in packaging and steel and composites in transport. That mechanism ties margin to the conversion premium per tonne, which is why Adjusted EBITDA per tonne, not margin on sales, is the right yardstick for revenue quality.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 12, 14; calculation C15
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Metal and other cost of goods sold, before depreciation, was 85.74% of net sales in the first half of fiscal 2027, so margin lives in a narrow conversion spread that is defended by pass-through but exposed to scrap spreads, energy, labour and tariffs. Natural gas and electricity were about 98% of energy cost, gas is bought on the open market, a majority of facilities have a unionized workforce, and a union strike at Yeongju in South Korea cut first-half production. The fixed-cost share of costs and the energy share of cost of goods sold are not stated, so operating leverage cannot be measured.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 47; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 18, 39; calculation C27

Margins can be defended against volume pressure and input shocks better than a margin on sales suggests: Adjusted EBITDA margin on net sales fell from 11.55% in fiscal 2024 to 8.84% over the last twelve months while net sales rose 27.75% and Adjusted EBITDA fell 2.24%, which is dilution from metal pass-through, not erosion of the conversion spread. The 2025 Efficiency Plan targets USD 350 million to USD 400 million of annual savings by fiscal 2028. A falling aluminum price would reverse the metal price lag gains of USD 574 million that reported earnings carry, but would also release working capital, so cash and reported earnings would move in opposite directions.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 47; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C15
### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Capital expenditure was USD 2,343 million in fiscal 2026, which is 12.71% of net sales, and USD 2,973 million over the last twelve months, 4.83 times depreciation and amortization, because of Bay Minette, a plant of about USD 5 billion and 600 kilotonnes of capacity that equals 16.87% of fiscal 2026 shipments. The issuer guides fiscal 2027 capital expenditure to USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.4 billion, including about USD 350 million of maintenance, and says it is phasing organic investment prudently, so maintenance is the floor and the rest is partly discretionary but largely committed to the plant. Remaining spend to complete the plant is not stated.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 110–112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 48, 65, 67; calculation C09; calculation C28

EBITDA has not converted to free cash flow: last-twelve-months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,831 million compares with operating cash flow of negative USD 1,022 million, because working capital, fire costs and start-up costs absorb cash that Adjusted EBITDA leaves out. Other cash claims are interest of USD 242 million paid in fiscal 2026, income taxes of USD 180 million, factoring expense of USD 73 million and expected pension contributions of USD 117 million in fiscal 2027. Capital spending could fall by 44.46% to 63.90% in the second half, but even then, if operating cash flow before working capital repeats the first half's USD 555 million, the half would fall short of breaking even by USD 2 million to USD 302 million before any working-capital release or insurance cash.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 112, 137, 159; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; calculation C09; calculation C11
### Porter's five forces

Rivalry is intense but structured by scale and qualification. The annual report lists competitors in each region, including Arconic, Constellium, Kaiser, Speira and several Chinese producers, states that the market is characterized by economies of scale and heavy capital investment, and says that customer qualification can take many months. Credit implication: a large installed base protects volumes, but low-priced exports from emerging markets and tariffs can move trade flows and press conversion premiums, as in the competition for scrap and the Section 232 effects the issuer reports.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 11–13

The threat of new entrants is low for flat-rolled sheet because a hot-mill plant costs billions of dollars, as Bay Minette shows at about USD 5 billion, and continuous casting is cheaper but serves a narrower product range. The threat of substitutes is moderate: aluminum has gained from glass, PET and steel on sustainability and weight, but the issuer notes that high aluminum prices can reverse that. Buyer power is high: the ten largest customers took 57% of fiscal 2026 net sales, Ball took 18%, some contracts carry no minimum volumes, and consolidation among customers increases their leverage. Supplier power is moderate: Rio Tinto, the primary metal supplier, was 6% of purchases in fiscal 2026, scrap is bought in a market where competition has risen, and gas is bought at market prices. Together, the forces cap pricing at the conversion premium and leave customer concentration as the main force that can move credit quality.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14, 17–18, 33, 188; calculation C23
### PEST analysis

Political and regulatory factors are material, because trade policy changes cost and trade flows directly. Section 232 tariffs of up to 50% apply to imported aluminum, a temporary 10% global surcharge was applied in February 2026, tariffs reduced fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA by USD 143 million, and the issuer cut Kingston production in September 2026 for at least six months to avoid duties. The US antidumping dispute over Brazilian shipments holds a cash deposit of about USD 127 million that the issuer considers remote to lose. Credit implication: tariffs depress North American margin and add freight and working-capital cost, and Kingston curtailment shows management will trade volume for margin.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 47; EX-99.1_2026-05-19_novelisq4fy26results.htm.jsonl, page 3

Economic and currency factors are also material: the euro, South Korean won, Brazilian real, Swiss franc and Canadian dollar move margins in the regions that sell or cost in them, and a 10% rise in the aluminum price would reduce the fair value of the metal derivatives by USD 324 million, a loss that the physical inventory offsets but that is settled in cash 30 to 90 days before customers pay. Interest rates matter less because a 100 bp rise would cut pre-tax income by about USD 15 million a year, although the USD 400 million of interest rate swaps run only to March 31, 2027. Social and technological factors, namely demand for recyclable packaging and scrap sorting technology, support volume and cost but do not move the near-term credit view.
### SWOT analysis

Strengths in credit terms are the pass-through pricing model, recycling integration with 62.41% recycled metal, regional diversification across four segments, a beverage packaging anchor at 54.45% of fiscal 2026 net sales, and demonstrated parent equity of USD 950 million. Weaknesses are negative adjusted free cash flow of USD 1,804 million in the half, leverage of 4.7x against a 3.5x target, revolver-dependent liquidity of USD 2,038 million, and customer concentration of 57% in the ten largest customers. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are Bay Minette reaching commercial shipments in the first quarter of fiscal 2028, the second-half fall in capital spending, continued insurance recoveries and the efficiency plan. Threats are a slip in the Bay Minette ramp, tariff escalation, a reversal of scrap spreads, a strike or plant outage, and the withdrawal of supplier finance or parent funding.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 47–48, 61; calculation C04; calculation C08; calculation C24
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are strong: net sales of USD 18,434 million, a presence in all four regions through 29 facilities, and a leading position in beverage and automotive sheet that the issuer states. Competitive advantage is average: qualification barriers and recycling integration help, but pricing power stops at the conversion premium. Business diversification is average: regions and end markets are diversified, but customers are concentrated. Cost and capex flexibility is average: maintenance spend of about USD 350 million is the floor and the plant spend can be phased, but the energy and fixed-cost shares are not disclosed. Margin stability is average: per-tonne earnings recovered but depend on scrap spreads, insurance and metal timing.

Free cash flow stability is weak: adjusted free cash flow was negative in each of the last three fiscal years and widened from USD 75 million negative in fiscal 2024 to USD 737 million negative in fiscal 2025 and USD 2,377 million negative in fiscal 2026. The ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: the issuer extended maturities and raised USD 1,975 million of new debt between June 2025 and July 2026, but no rating, price or spread is supplied, so market access is read from the transactions completed. Liquidity position is average, and falling: USD 2,038 million, with a revolver maturing in 2031. Financial policy and governance is average: equity-supportive and transparent with a stated leverage goal, but the goal is exceeded, the owner controls the Board, and no guarantee is stated. The trend is deteriorating in cash terms and improving in earnings terms; the missing datapoints are covenant calculations, ratings, a peer set, the remaining Bay Minette spend and the second-half cash flow plan.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–23, 61; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C04
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next twelve to twenty-four months the decisive facts are the second-half step-down in capital spending, the Bay Minette ramp, and the flow of insurance recoveries. Management guides to positive free cash flow in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, deleveraging toward the end of the fiscal year, and commercial Bay Minette shipments in the first quarter of fiscal 2028, and it has kept the same timing, the end of fiscal 2027, at each of three reporting dates, in May, August and November 2026. Tailwinds are favorable scrap pricing, the Oswego restart in June 2026, recoveries still to come, and demand in beverage and aerospace. Headwinds are higher net tariffs, the Yeongju strike, weaker automotive and specialty shipments in the second quarter, and the expiry of the interest rate swaps in March 2027. Each tailwind lifts cash flow and each headwind lengthens the period of revolver use.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-19_novelisq4fy26results.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_novelisq1fy27results.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 29, 46–48

Over three to five years the credit depends on whether 600 kilotonnes of new North American capacity is filled at a conversion margin that supports the debt added to build it. The issuer expects growing long-term demand for beverage cans, automotive lightweighting and aerospace plate, but the annual report also notes that material substitution and tariffs can shift volume. The 2029 to 2031 maturities fall in this window, so the plant's contribution to Adjusted EBITDA has to be visible before those refinancings. A capacity addition of 16.87% of fiscal 2026 shipments can lift Adjusted EBITDA materially if it ramps, and keep leverage high if it does not.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46, 67; 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; calculation C22; calculation C28
### Downside scenario

The most plausible downside path is a slow Bay Minette ramp combined with metal prices that stay high, and it runs through working capital and the revolver, not through earnings collapse. The initiating condition is commercial shipments slipping beyond the first quarter of fiscal 2028 or ramping slowly while aluminum stays near USD 3,204 per tonne and the local premium near USD 1,242. The first operational break is that start-up costs, which Adjusted EBITDA excludes, and capital spending at the top of the USD 2.1 billion to USD 2.4 billion range persist. The financial transmission is that operating cash flow stays negative as inventories absorb cash, as they did in the first half when they took USD 733 million, so adjusted free cash flow stays negative and the revolver funds it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 48–49, 65; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9

The consequence is that availability falls from USD 606 million toward the USD 300 million that the annual report's formula implies for the current commitment, at which a minimum fixed charge ratio of 1.25 to 1.0 would apply, a distance of USD 306 million if the wording is unchanged, and the issuer's net leverage ratio rises above 4.7x because Adjusted EBITDA does not grow into the debt. Management levers are lower discretionary capital spending, working capital release if metal prices fall, more insurance proceeds, the USD 800 million of uncommitted lines, and parent equity, none of which is committed. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis within twelve months if capital spending falls as guided, because the 6.78 months of runway at the first-half pace assumes no fall in spending and the revolver does not mature until 2031, but it is not sufficient to bring leverage back to the target unless the plant ramps. The observable triggers are availability below USD 300 million, a third-quarter adjusted free cash outflow, and a slip in the commercial shipment date.
Basis: 10-K_2026-03-31_nvl-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 148; 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C06; calculation C11; calculation C12
### Credit quality factors and primary downside path

Revenue durability is average: pass-through pricing and a beverage anchor are offset by customer concentration. Margin resilience is average: per-tonne earnings recovered but include insurance and scrap benefits. Free cash flow conversion is weak. The liquidity buffer is average, and falling. Refinancing capacity is average: tenor was extended, but there is no rating or market evidence. Governance and financial policy are average: supportive, controlled by the parent, with a leverage goal that is currently exceeded.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_nvl-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 65; calculation C04; calculation C08

Primary downside path: a delay in Bay Minette commercial shipments keeps free cash flow negative, revolver availability falls toward its test level, and leverage stays above the target as the 2029 to 2031 maturities approach.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_novelisq2fy27results.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C06; calculation C22
### Overall credit view

Overall, Novelis presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, pass-through pricing, recycling integration and regional diversification, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow, leverage of 4.7x against a 3.5x target and revolver-dependent liquidity. Cash-flow durability appears weak in the near term and adequate if capital spending falls as guided, because EBITDA has not yet converted to cash. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the Bay Minette ramp, on leverage falling toward the target before 2029 to 2031, and on parent support that is not committed. The primary downside path is a delay in commercial shipments that keeps cash flow negative while the revolver funds it. The business profile cannot be benchmarked against typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector because no peer set was supplied; a more definitive opinion would need covenant calculations, ratings, the second-half cash flow plan and the remaining plant spend. Credit view completed. Top risk: negative free cash flow until Bay Minette ships commercially.
